blocks.text: …she found his first wife's Facebook page three weeks ago."
The manager, a calm woman named Gloria, dialed the number at the bottom of the email. It was my daughter's cell. Emily answered on the first ring. "Mom? Are you okay? Did you sign anything?"
"Don't go back to the table," she said. "I'm in the parking lot."
Emily had never been working late. She'd been sitting in her car outside the restaurant for two hours, waiting for Gloria to call.

Three weeks earlier, while looking for a tax document in Brandon's desk, Emily had found a divorce decree from Nevada. Brandon had told her he'd never been married. She searched for the ex-wife's name online and found her: a woman named Rachel in Reno. Rachel agreed to talk.

She told Emily that Brandon had persuaded her widowed mother to sign "tax-saving" documents during a nice dinner. The papers turned out to be a quitclaim deed and a power of attorney. Within six months, her mother's house had been refinanced, the money was gone, and so was Brandon. Rachel's mother lost her home. Rachel had reported him to the police, but the case stalled when he left the state.
The photo in the email was Brandon with Rachel at their wedding in 2015.

Emily didn't confront Brandon. She was afraid he'd simply move faster. Instead, she called a lawyer and an investigator, and when Brandon told her he was taking me out for my birthday, she guessed exactly what he was planning. She called the restaurant, explained everything, and asked them to watch.
When I walked out to the parking lot, Emily hugged me so tight I couldn't breathe.
A police officer was standing next to her car. Inside, Gloria asked Brandon to wait for "a manager's discount." He was still waiting, holding his folder, when the officer walked up to the table.
The documents in the folder were a quitclaim deed for my house and a power of attorney over my retirement accounts.

Brandon was charged with attempted fraud in Arizona, and Nevada reopened the case involving Rachel's mother. He pleaded guilty to both the following year. Emily filed for divorce the week after the dinner.
Rachel and her mother came to Scottsdale for my seventieth birthday. We ate at the same steakhouse. Gloria brought out a cake. There were no folders on the table, only candles.
